title: Dry-run: fan-out on write, then the hybrid
intro: About 6 minutes. Write the push version, break it on a celebrity account, then show the hybrid. The break is the part interviewers are waiting for.

steps.title: Establish the ratio first
steps.explain: Lead with the read:write ratio, because it decides the whole design. Two orders of magnitude more reads than writes says do the work at write time so reads stay cheap.
steps.saysOutLoud: Reads outnumber writes about a hundred to one, so I'll pay at write time.

steps.title: The write path, without fan-out inline
steps.explain: Persist once, then enqueue. Doing fan-out inside the request would make the author wait for millions of writes — the queue is what keeps their response fast while the work happens behind them.

steps.title: The fan-out worker
steps.explain: Insert the post id into every follower's feed list, trimmed so lists cannot grow without bound. Note it stores ids, not post bodies — so editing or deleting a post never means rewriting millions of feeds.
steps.saysOutLoud: Feeds hold ids only. The post itself is stored once and hydrated on read.

steps.title: The read path is now trivial
steps.explain: One cache read plus a hydrate. No joins, no merging across sources, no ranking over unbounded input — which is exactly the payoff for having paid at write time.

steps.title: Break it with a celebrity
steps.explain: One post becoming ten million cache writes saturates the workers and delays fan-out for everyone else on the queue. The system's worst case is triggered by its most visible users — say that plainly before offering the fix.
steps.saysOutLoud: Ten million followers means one action becomes ten million writes. That's the ceiling.

steps.title: Split by follower count
steps.explain: The pathological case is a small, identifiable set of accounts — so handle it with a different mechanism instead of making every user pay. Skip fan-out above a threshold and merge those posts at read time.

steps.title: Merge the celebrity posts on read
steps.explain: Most users get a fully precomputed feed and pay nothing extra. A read costs one cache lookup plus a small merge from the handful of high-follower accounts that user follows — bounded, because nobody follows thousands of celebrities.
steps.saysOutLoud: Precomputed feed plus a small merge — the expensive case scales with the mechanism that handles it.

steps.title: Use cursor pagination, not offset
steps.explain: A feed has items inserted at the head between page loads, so OFFSET shifts and users see duplicates or gaps. Cursor pagination is stable under insertion, and roughly time-sortable ids are what make it work — the same ids from the unique-ID topic.

steps.title: Ranking belongs on the read path
steps.explain: Precompute the candidate set with fan-out, then score a few hundred candidates per request using engagement signals and affinity. Ranking at write time would mean re-ranking every follower's feed whenever any signal changes, which is unbounded work — the same shape as the autocomplete split between candidate generation and per-request personalisation.

closing: If they push on storage: capping each feed list at ~800 ids bounds memory per user, and anything older is served by falling back to a query rather than the cache.
